rgeodesy

R bindings to Rust Geodesy (RG) by Thomas Knudsen — a platform for experiments with geodetic transformations and data flow. You build a transformation by writing a pipeline string of named operators and apply it to vectors of coordinates.

RG is a geodesy library rather than a cartography library: its datum and reference-frame machinery is extensive, and it supports a focused, high-quality set of map projections. It is well suited to learning the RG architecture and to geodetic operations that are awkward in PROJ-based tooling.

Installation

rgeodesy compiles a small Rust crate at install time, so you need a Rust toolchain (install via rustup, rustc >= 1.87):

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("hypertidy/rgeodesy")

Quick start 

library(rgeodesy)

# Geographic (lon, lat) in degrees -> UTM zone 55 south (easting, northing).
geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = c(147.3, 147.5), y = c(-42.9, -42.8))
#> $x
#> [1] 524492.1 540886.1
#> $y
#> [1] 5250246 5261273

# The same thing as a two-column matrix.
geod_xy("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = c(147.3, 147.5), y = c(-42.9, -42.8))
#>             x       y
#> [1,] 524492.1 5250246
#> [2,] 540886.1 5261273

# Inverse: projected -> geographic (set inv = TRUE on the forward pipeline).
m <- geod_xy("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = 147.3, y = -42.9)
geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = m[, "x"], y = m[, "y"], inv = TRUE)
#> $x
#> [1] 147.3
#> $y
#> [1] -42.9

How transformations are specified

Rust Geodesy does not use EPSG codes or a from -> to pair of CRSs. Instead you describe the transformation directly as a pipeline of operator primitives, chained with |, each taking key=value arguments:

gis:in | utm zone=32 | gis:out

Because RG works internally in radians with a geodetic axis order, geographic data is bracketed with an I/O adaptor:

Adaptor Units Order Use for
gis:in / gis:out degrees (lon, lat) natural (x, y) — recommended
geo:in / geo:out degrees (lat, lon) geodetic latitude-first
enu:in / neu:in radians east/north-first already-radian input

Validate a pipeline before using it:

geod_validate("gis:in | utm zone=55 south")   # TRUE
geod_validate("utm zone=banana")              # "Failed to build op ...: Malformed value ..."

Operator families (Rust Geodesy 0.15)

geod_ops() returns the full list of registered operators. The main families:

Family Operators
Projections utm, tmerc, btmerc/butm (Bowring series), merc, webmerc, lcc, laea, omerc, somerc
Datum / reference-frame cart, helmert, molodensky, gridshift, deformation
Geodetic computations geodesic, curvature, gravity, latitude, deflection, permtide
Adaptors & units adapt, axisswap, unitconvert, dm, dms, geo:*/gis:*/neu:*/enu:*, noop

See the Rust Geodesy operator documentation for the arguments each operator accepts.

Current limitations

  • The interface passes two coordinates (x, y) per point. Operators that are inherently three-dimensional (cart, helmert, deformation) need a height component to round-trip correctly, so full 3-D datum transforms are not yet usable through this 2-D interface. Projections and 2-D operators work as expected.
  • This is early, experimental software; the API may change.
